name: Pastitsio (Greek Ground Beef and Pasta Casserole)

ingredients.name: egg yolks, at room temperature, lightly beaten
packed roughly chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves, tender stems

instructions.primary_message: For the Meat Sauce: In a medium saucepan, heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion and 1 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add beef, pork, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt and cook, breaking meat into small pieces with a wooden spoon or stiff spatula, until no longer pink, 5 to 7 minutes.

Add tomato paste, miso, pumpkin spice or cinnamon, oregano, thyme, and marjoram (if using), and cook, stirring constantly, until the paste evenly coats the meat and the spices are fragrant, about 1 minute. Add wine and cook, stirring and scraping up any browned bits from bottom of saucepan, until wine is almost completely evaporated, about 3 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, bay leaves, and 1/4 cup water and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce is slightly thickened and flavors have melded, 15 to 18 minutes. Remove from heat, discard bay leaves, and skim and discard any excess fat from surface. Set aside to cool slightly.

For the Pasta: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). In a large pot of boiling water, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well, then transfer to a 9- by 33-cm baking dish. Add oil and toss to coat. Spread pasta into an even layer and set aside to cool slightly.

For the Béchamel: In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, add flour, and cook, stirring constantly with a flexible spatula and scraping bottom and sides of saucepan, until mixture no longer smells like raw flour but remains pale, 1 to 2 minutes.

Whisking constantly, gradually add milk in roughly 1/2-cup increments, whisking until completely smooth after each addition. Once all milk is incorporated, increase heat to medium and cook, stirring constantly with a flexible spatula and scraping bottom and sides of saucepan, until béchamel is smooth, creamy, and thick enough to coat the spatula. Remove from heat.
Whisk salt and pepper into béchamel. Add Gruyère a small handful at a time, whisking until melted and smooth after each addition. Add egg yolks and whisk until thoroughly combined. Set aside.

For Assembly: Add parsley, oregano, and beaten egg to cooled pasta in baking dish and toss until evenly coated. Rearrange pasta in an even layer. Stir 1/2 cup béchamel into meat sauce, then spoon meat sauce over pasta in an even layer. Ladle remaining béchamel over meat sauce and gently spread into an even layer, trying to keep sauce layers distinct. Sprinkle evenly with Gruyère or Parmesan.

Set baking dish on a rimmed baking sheet and bake until top is golden brown and edges are bubbling, 40 to 45 minutes. For deeper browning, switch oven to broil and cook, watching carefully, until top is browned to your liking, 1 to 3 minutes.
Let pastitsio cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing and serving.

schema_metadata.keywords: Pastitsio, Greek Ground Beef and Pasta Casserole, 9x13 casserole recipe

description: Learn how to make pastitsio, a crowd-pleasing Greek 9x13 casserole layered with savory ground beef, pasta, and creamy béchamel—perfect for making ahead.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1/2 teaspoon dried marjoram (optional)

Optional substitutions: pumpkin spice mix → ground cinnamon; dried bay leaves → fresh bay leaves; whole cow’s milk → goat’s milk; pastitsio noodles → penne or ziti; Gruyère cheese → Parmesan cheese

Notes: Pastitsio noodles are long, hollow Greek pasta noodles available at Greek and other Mediterranean markets and online. If unavailable, substitute penne or ziti. If using long pastitsio noodles, break them as needed to fit the baking dish.
Kefalotyri and kefalograviera are traditionally used in pastitsio but can be difficult to find in the US. If available, either may be substituted for the Gruyère or Parmesan. Because these cheeses vary in saltiness, adjust the seasoning as needed.

Make-ahead and storage: The meat sauce can be prepared up to 3 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container.
Leftover pastitsio can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days. To freeze, cool the pastitsio completely, cut it into individual portions, and wrap each portion tightly in plastic wrap, then aluminum foil, or transfer it to airtight, freezer-safe containers. Freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating. You can also freeze the entire casserole, though individual portions are easier to store and reheat.
author: Sharon Brenner
